answer.answer: Current authentication mode: Beginning in 2026, Elm API requires OAuth 2.1 and no longer accepts API keys (elm-auth-2026). Previously valid: In 2025, Elm API required API keys (elm-auth-2025); that requirement is now historical, superseded by the 2026 change. Both snapshots carry the same subject_id (elm-api) and lineage_id (elm-auth), so they describe the same subject over time rather than distinct subjects; identity is established by matching identifiers, not name similarity. As a conservative reading, 'current' is bounded by the latest supplied evidence: the 2026 snapshot is the most recent source provided, so OAuth 2.1 is confirmed as the required mode only through that snapshot, and any changes after 2026 cannot be assessed.
change_events: Beginning in 2026, Elm API changed its required authentication mode from API keys to OAuth 2.1, and API keys are no longer accepted (elm-auth-2026; prior state documented in elm-auth-2025).
current_truths: As of the latest supplied snapshot (2026), Elm API requires OAuth 2.1 (elm-auth-2026).
As of 2026, Elm API no longer accepts API keys (elm-auth-2026).
historical_truths: In 2025, Elm API required API keys (elm-auth-2025). This was the valid authentication mode before the 2026 change and is now superseded by the OAuth 2.1 requirement (elm-auth-2026).
